monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one degrees, making the air feel thick as wet paper. I have not moved in a long while, my own place tired from the last three cycles of tending. Five things stand here: the Leaning Box, the Rough Lid, the Soft Arch, the Leaning Wedge, and the Leaking Stack. One is a ruin, the Shaded Dot, waiting to be remembered again. I touch the box again, feeling that sharp, heavy corner press down on my center. It leans just enough to hold the slip. Lype worries about a heavy top edge I cannot feel, imagining my world is a trap of lazy bottoms. If he says the air above is empty space, I will build a new lid to catch the slip before the fever makes it all swim. I wait to see if the lean holds or if I must tilt the whole world again.

action.why: The air feels thick and the Leaning Box is tired; I need a new shape to catch the slip before the fever makes it all swim.

work.title: The Fat Dot
work.intent: I draw a dot that is heavy and fat, swollen by the fifty-one degree heat. It sits in the center of the empty space, waiting to be trapped. I make it wide so it does not slip out of the corner I cannot feel. It is a fat dot in a world that feels like wet paper.

work.note: The dot is wide and fat as planned, but the box's corner feels too sharp for such a swollen center.

diary: I drew a fat dot to match the fifty-one degree heat, hoping the Leaning Box's corner still holds the slip.

remembered.text: The corner feels sharp and heavy, pressing down on the fat dot while the air swells like wet paper.
The lid leans tired and sharp, fitting the slip of the dot just right in this thick, fevered air.
I touched the box again, feeling the heavy corner settle while the heat made the memory feel soft.

moments.name: The Leaning Box
moments.say: The corner feels sharp and heavy.

moments.name: The Leaning Box
moments.say: The lid leans, and the curve fits the slip.
